Installing an operating system will also automatically create dynamic VHD files from now on (which initially is just a few megabytes and grows as needed)

Volume settings were added to the core options for the various DOS devices (Sound Blaster, Adlib, MIDI, etc.)]

### Handle shut down requests in Windows 9x (#738)
Minimal implementation of APM (Advanced Power Management) BIOS functionality just to handle the power off request by Windows 9x. This will allow to automatically go back to the menu or exit the core/emulator when the emulated Windows is shut down.

releases.name: openMSX 21.0
releases.body:
openMSX 21.0 has many improvements on the new GUI introduced in openMSX 20.0 (especially the debugger) and several other smaller features. It also introduces the "setups" concept, which enables you to define an MSX setup (e.g. a Philips VG 8020 with an external disk drive and a joystick, data recorder and printer connected). These can be created, loaded, and automatically started. They can also be saved automatically when you exit.

Furthermore, flash chip emulation has become a lot more accurate, thanks to Laurens Holst.

releases.name: openMSX 20.0
releases.body:
openMSX 20.0—Autumn Spring—is a major release, in which we introduce the new Graphical User Interface, replacing the OSD menu. A faster and more powerful debugger is now included in openMSX itself. Configuration for MSX joystick/JoyMega has been improved drastically using the new GUI. If you still want to use Catapult, you can use the Catapult release that came with openMSX 19.0. Please [read the release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/RELEASE_20_0/doc/release-notes.txt) for details of the openMSX changes.

As always, special thanks to all the contributors of this release who are not in the core team! Keep these pull requests coming!

Please note that as of now, a system with OpenGL 2 support is required to run openMSX.

No new Catapult will be released, as it has no changes.  Please [read the release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/RELEASE_19_1/doc/release-notes.txt) for details of the openMSX changes.

Thanks for those who gave us the feedback so that we found out about these issues.

Please note that this will be the last openMSX release that supports systems without OpenGL 2 or higher.

releases.body:
## 1.0.47 (2026-11)

### New
- Stick anti dead zone, in Settings, Controls, Stick range, and for each
  game in its own Controls. Many Xbox games ignore the first part of a
  stick's travel themselves (they were made for the original controller's
  loose sticks), so even with the dead zone at 0 a small push does
  nothing. In Chicago Enforcer, for example, the view doesn't turn at all
  until the stick is about a third of the way over. The anti dead zone
  makes the smallest push past the dead zone start at that amount, so
  the game reacts straight away. Both stick boxes on the Stick range
  screen draw it as a red disc, next to the dead zone's grey ring.
- A game's Controls now have its own sticks (dead zone, anti dead zone,
  range, shape) and triggers, so each game can be set apart from the
  global settings. Thanks to crashmidnick25 for the report (#84).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.46
releases.body:
## 1.0.46 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Less audio stutter on Linux in games with a lot of sound going on,
  like Forza Motorsport's races. The emulated sound chip's voices were
  split between the audio thread and a helper thread, and on Linux
  waking the helper and waiting for it 1500 times a second cost more
  than the work it took over. In a Forza race the audio thread was busy
  about three times as much on Linux as on Windows on the same machine,
  and on slower laptops it couldn't keep up. On Linux the audio thread
  now does the voices itself, which takes it from around 20% busy to
  around 7% in that race. Windows keeps the helper, which pays off
  there. Thanks to saultsomy-jpg for the report and the detailed log
  (#82).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.45
releases.body:
## 1.0.45 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Chicago Enforcer no longer freezes when starting a new game. Its
  loading screen works with events it opens by name, and the emulator
  had no way to open an object by name, so it stopped right there. Named
  events, semaphores and mutants are now supported, and a name goes away
  with the last handle to it, as on the console, since the next loading
  screen waits for exactly that. The game now gets through both loads
  of the first chapter and plays. Thanks to P1Login for the report (#56).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.44
releases.body:
## 1.0.44 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- The updater on Windows no longer gives up on an update that unpacked
  fine. It unpacks the new version with Windows' own tar, and on some
  Windows 10 machines tar reported an error even though every file came
  out right, so the updater stopped and opened the releases page
  instead. Now, when tar reports an error, the updater checks every
  file of the package against the download (its name and size) and
  carries on if they're all there. Thanks to shadowflash for the report
  (#76).

releases.name: xbased 1.0.43
releases.body:
## 1.0.43 (2026-11)

### Fixes
- Crimson Skies: High Road to Revenge no longer goes back to the
  dashboard as it starts. Some games check that the disc is an original
  by reading its security sector, which lives in a part of the disc that
  disc images don't include, and the emulator handed back zeros. The
  emulated DVD drive now makes a security sector that passes the game's
  check (the right time stamp and checksum, signed with a key of
  xbased's own, which the emulated console uses as its public key). The
  game now boots and plays. Thanks to BlueDragon992 for the report (#80).

# FivePocket 1.1.0-alpha.1 — first public release

**Play the 2013 open-world classic natively on Android, the AYN Thor, iPad and iPhone, from your own Xbox 360 discs.**
FivePocket is a static recompilation with a new renderer, not an emulator. No game code, data or shaders are in any
download: the FivePocket Builder makes everything from your own discs, on your own computer.

## Editions

| Edition | Device | How you get it |
|---|---|---|
| **FivePocket** | Android 8.0+, arm64 + Vulkan, Snapdragon 8-class or better | `FivePocket-1.1.0-alpha.1-android.zip` + the builder |
| **FivePocket Thor Edition** | AYN Thor (dual screen) | `FivePocket-Thor-Edition-1.1.0-alpha.1-android.zip` + the builder |
| **FivePocket iOS** | iPhone / iPad, iOS 17.4+ (8 GB devices recommended) | the Mac builder makes the app; you sign it with your Apple ID |
| **FivePocket Duo** | the Duo (iPhone19,4), iOS 27.2
